text:
Jorge: quick heads up — ran a param sweep on eviction hysteresis for tenant fairness and found some surprising tail behaviors. notes below.
Hannah: nice, paste numbers?
Jorge: TL;DR: aggressive hysteresis (long grace window) reduces churn but amplifies cold-start latency for small tenants; short hysteresis reduces cold startup but causes noisy tenants to hoard slab space.
Mira: classic tradeoff. what metrics did you record?
Jorge: measured slab-occupancy-variance, p50/p95 read latency on cold prefixes, and evict-induced-retries. key datapoints:
- hysteresis=2000ms: occupancy variance low, cold p95 +18ms, evict-retries minimal
- hysteresis=200ms: occupancy variance high, cold p95 +4ms, evict-retries +34%
Ben: how are you defining evict-induced-retries?
Jorge: read attempts that fell back to authoritative after eviction then returned and retried local path. essentially extra latency work from races.
Hannah: do we have correlation with tenant hotness? noisy tenants (high QPS) got better qos with long hysteresis, small tenants suffered.
Mira: any distribution skew? e.g. tail dominated by extremely small prefixes?
Jorge: yes, 80/20: 20% of prefixes (hot) account for 70% of slab footprint under short hysteresis; long hysteresis evens it out but keeps cold prefixes offline longer.
Ben: operationally, can we make hysteresis adaptive by prefix hotness? like hysteresis = base + alpha * hot_score.
Mira: that seems promising. set base low to avoid long cold-starts, add extra window for hot prefixes to reduce churn. how compute hot_score cheaply? maybe time-decayed QPS or LRU recency bucket.
Hannah: watch out for oscillation: if hysteresis grows with hotness, a prefix that appears hot will lock itself in longer. need damping and max cap.
Jorge: proposal: hysteresis_ms = clamp(base_ms + scale * log(1+hot_qps), min_ms, max_ms). default base=150ms, scale=300ms, min=50ms, max=3000ms.
Ben: log helps smooth; good. also add hysteresis_backoff when eviction fails repeatedly: reduce hysteresis to force reclamation.
Mira: testing plan: bench three rings — small-tenant heavy, noisy-tenant heavy, mixed. compare memory churn, tail-latency, and eviction retries.
Jorge: I'll implement as feature-flagged experiment runtime.flags.adaptive_hysteresis=true with canary rings. add metrics: prefix.hysteresis_ms, prefix.hysteresis_adjust_events, prefix.evict_retries.
Hannah: add alert if median hysteresis across a node > 1500ms and evict_retries > 10% — might indicate hoarding.
Ben: one more thought: combine with soft-evict grace per-tenant credit bucket so noisy tenants pay eviction cost over time. adaptive hysteresis + credits could balance fairness.
Mira: agree. keep approach incremental: land adaptive hysteresis first, bake for two weeks, then add credit layer.
ci-bot: created EXP-evict-523: "adaptive-hysteresis canary" assigned to @jorge, due 2026-04-15 :white_check_mark:
Hannah: thanks Jorge, this would be great to tame churn without killing cold-starts.
Jorge: will open RFC note after canary results with perf tables. ETA preliminary numbers next Wed.
